question: A knowledge base tool asks Claude to answer users' questions using only information retrieved from company documents, and the team wants every claim traceable to the exact retrieved passage it came from. Which technique best supports this analysis and answering task?
options: A) Have Claude answer directly from memory instead of using the retrieved documents at all
B) Have Claude answer first and only fetch supporting documents afterward instead
C) Have Claude paraphrase only the general topic of the documents, not any passage
D) Have Claude quote the specific passages from the retrieved documents before answering
correct_answers: D) Have Claude quote the specific passages from the retrieved documents before answering
explanations: Incorrect. Answering from memory instead of the retrieved documents does not produce claims traceable to specific retrieved passages.
Incorrect. Answering before retrieving documents reverses the order needed to ground the answer in the actual retrieved passages.
Incorrect. A general paraphrase without quoting specific passages does not give the traceability to exact source text that the team needs.

Correct. Grounding responses in quotes, having Claude quote relevant passages before answering, helps produce traceable, source-grounded answers, which fits the requirement that every claim be traceable to a passage.
